title: Goal Atelier — Reflective Dossier
content:
Purpose: lightweight single-page atelier for tracking progress on a small set of personal commitments. Not formal OKRs yet — experiments first. Notes to self, decisions, and planned micro-experiments.

Quick summary (one-liner): Move from reactive task lists to a steady 3x weekly output cycle that meaningfully reduces my context-switching and increases two measurable outcomes: (1) feature throughput (merged PRs per week) and (2) time blocked on infra/ops issues.

Why this matters right now:
- Q1 has been noisy: on-call spikes, ad-hoc meetings, and two feature rollouts. Hard to get deep focus.
- If I don't create small constraints and cadence, the backlog becomes a queue of half-done experiments.
- I want to model better habits for junior engineers on my squad — show how to structure a micro-OKR and stick to it.

Current anchors (3 commitments):
1) Ship three small improvements to the rollout UI (console) by end of March.
   - outcome metric: 3 merged PRs labeled "rollout-ui" or "console-improve".
   - success signal: at least one A/B test candidate prepared and one rollout doc drafted.
2) Reduce weekly time blocked by infra/ops (SRE tickets) from ~6h to <=2h.
   - outcome metric: average time-to-resolution for my assigned infra tickets.
   - success signal: adopt a recurring 30-min weekly triage window and handoffs documented.
3) Start a 4-week habit of focused writing (20–30m daily) about learnings.
   - outcome metric: 15 short notes (>=200 words) by end of 4 weeks.
   - success signal: first note converted into a short team playbook section.

Hypotheses (things to test):
- H1: Dedicated triage block on Tuesday mornings will reduce incident context switching and lower time blocked by ~50%.
- H2: Constraining PR scope to a "one-change-per-PR" rule will increase merge rate and reduce rework.
- H3: A short daily writing habit improves clarity in PR descriptions and reduces review cycles by at least one round.

Experiments (planned week-by-week):
Week A (Feb 16–22)
- Block Tue 09:00–09:30 for infra triage (calendar invite: infra-triage).
- Do 3 small console UI mockups, open 1 PR by Friday.
- Daily write: 15 mins, capture one friction noticed during the day.
Data to capture: PR open/merge timestamps, time spent on triage, note count.

Week B (Feb 23–Mar 01)
- Enforce "one-change-per-PR" for console improvements.
- Measure average review rounds and time-to-merge.
- Try A/B test scaffold doc for 1 candidate feature.

Week C (Mar 02–08)
- If triage block helped, run it again and invite SRE buddy.
- Convert two top friction notes into a mini playbook draft.

Metrics dashboard (manual for now):
- PR throughput: count(PRs merged labeled console-improve) per week.
- Time blocked: sum(hours) logged on SRE/infra tickets assigned to me per week.
- Review rounds: average number of review cycles until merge for console PRs.
- Writing streak: consecutive days with >=15 minutes of writing.

Short retrospective — current snapshot (Mar 10)
- What worked:
  - Triage block reduced pings during deep work blocks — felt less reactive.
  - "One-change-per-PR" forced smaller diffs; reviewers were happier.
- What didn't:
  - Daily writing habit is inconsistent (5/23 days so far).
  - Context for infra tickets still leaks into feature work when on-call spikes.
- Quick wins to try immediately:
  - Move triage block to a recurring shared invite with SRE as a standing sync.
  - Pre-PR checklist template to capture test plan and rollback strategy (reduces back-and-forth).

Unresolved questions / risks:
- Risk: feature velocity might slow if PR fragmentation creates too many small merges — need balance.
- Can I get manager buy-in to reserve "no meeting" afternoons two days a week? (ask on 1:1 3/12)
- How to measure time blocked more accurately without overinstrumenting (ideally use ticket worklog tags).

Decisions & next actions (concrete):
- ACTION 01 (by 2026-03-12): Draft pre-PR checklist and add to PR template. (owner: me)
- ACTION 02 (by 2026-03-15): Add SRE to triage block and set shared agenda (owner: me + Zoe Lin)
- ACTION 03 (by 2026-03-22): Convert 4 diary notes to a single "Console rollout playbook" draft. (owner: me + Maya Shah)

Notes to self (quick heuristics):
- If a task will take <=1.5 hours, do it in the same day. If >1.5 hours, schedule a dedicated deep block.
- PR rule: 1 change, 1 test, 1 short description — avoid multi-feature PRs.
- Use the writing habit to force slow thinking: 3 paragraphs = 1 clear next step.

Reference links / shortcuts: (store here for quick paste)
- Confluence: team playbook (link: confluence:team-playbook-824)
- Relevant JIRA tickets: INF-903, FEAT-1221
- PR template snippet: github:ryan-yu/personal-okr-notes#pr-template

Weekly check-in template (use for the next 6 weeks)
- Wins (2)
- Blockers (1)
- Metrics snapshot (PRs merged / time blocked / review rounds)
- One adjustment for the next week

Closing thought: small constraints + a short writing habit should amplify signal in the weeks ahead. Keep this doc minimal, iterate weekly, and convert any reproducible practice into a team playbook.

-- ryan

(P.S. If this lives longer than a quarter, convert to a proper OKR format and add owner-level success criteria.)
